record.title: Read and prepare the first RF pilot settings through SCPI
record.intent: Replace manual setting reports with retained instrument readback while the source remains off.
requirements: Bind this operation to the operator-confirmed RF OUT to CH1 connection, 50-ohm termination and source-off state, and the explicit request to use SCPI for setup.

Revalidate the isolated Ethernet interface and restore only its temporary host address and single-client six-hour DHCP lease as needed. Preserve baseline and cleanup evidence, with no gateway, DNS, bridging, forwarding or NAT.

Start a fresh full packet capture before introducing the address or DHCP. Require readiness, graceful termination and retained drop statistics. Stop on recorder failure or unexpected network behavior.

Use the official programming guide and the established SCPI socket only. Preserve raw identity and channel, acquisition, timebase and trigger queries before any setting changes; make only documented ordinary settings needed for a CH1 100 MHz pilot and read them back.

Keep the source powered off. Do not use ADB, change firmware or entitlements, perform calibration, reset defaults, reboot, scan services or change persistent network settings. A connection failure is a preserved result, not authority for a broader trial.
Seal private evidence, keep unit identifiers and host details out of source, and commit and push the bounded conclusion.
acceptance: Instrument readback establishes the pilot setup or a precise connection/setup blocker is preserved without an RF measurement claim.
